_comment: A0-random of docs/2026-09-07_anytime_prediction_and_calibrated_eta_design.zh.md §2.2: the arm that reads the re-anchoring curve WITHOUT the distribution-shift cost. Every existing checkpoint was trained at the L-1 anchor only, so A0-fixed's later bins are out-of-distribution (the closure arm's 12 km vectored ADE went 2197 -> 6706 m in the review's replay). random_train_anchor=True trains at one uniformly random valid anchor per flight and epoch (min 60 s of future). The imitation teachers are anchor-bound (the inverse-dynamics one is a recorded performance cliff under random anchors, the fitted table is fitted at L-1), so the only screened supervision compatible with random anchors is L1.b's teacherless combination: heading-rate 8 + bank TV 1 (60-epoch screen: bank skill 0.711 vs the teacher control's 0.709, ADE not worse). Same base as l1b_full_arms.json, 180 epochs. READING (design doc §2.4): replay this checkpoint with run_ts_anytime_curve.py on the same remaining-path grid as A0-fixed, paired per flight and stratum with L1_native32 (fixed) — the difference at each bin is the distribution-shift cost, the shape of the A0-random curve is the anytime deliverable. VETO: A0-random at the L-1 bin worse than L1_native32 beyond seed noise (random-anchor training damaged the base). Known limit stated in advance: the duration head's ~125 s floor means |dt| p80 cannot fall under 30 s near the runway for ANY arm here; s_freeze is read where it can be, and the floor is the B-line's problem (quantile head).

arms.label: random train anchors + hr=8 + TV=1 (no teacher), 180 epochs
